target_customer: Single-family rental and small multifamily property management companies
problem: Property managers spend a large share of their day coordinating maintenance requests and emergencies, including after hours.
business_model: B2B SaaS and service fees: per account fee plus per unit per month, with maintenance coordination services
product_category: Property maintenance coordination, now an AI front office for property managers

founders.name: Ethan Lieber
founders.background_notes: YC page: previously Director of Product at OPO managing lead generation products for home services.

founders.name: Will Gordon
founders.background_notes: Inman (2019-06-19) says he worked at Amazon while managing an inherited family real estate portfolio, which led him to approach Lieber.

founders.name: Jullian Chavez
founders.background_notes: Named as a co-founder in the GeekWire 2022 photo caption; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Software for ticketing, vendor dispatch and tenant communication on standard stack; the hard part was operating a human call and vendor network around the clock.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with property management systems and a vetted contractor network of over 3,000 (TechCrunch 2019-02-22) raise switching costs, but the software itself was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Property management systems later offered maintenance modules and Latchel integrated with them (Yardi, AppFolio, Buildium, Rent Manager listed on its site) rather than being displaced; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Inman 2019 quotes the founders saying managers spent up to 45 percent of the day on maintenance coordination; TechCrunch Feb 2019 reports 27,500 units across 50 cities and growth of 4,000 to 5,000 units per month.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident, outcome-focused with short punchy lines (company site)

brand_strength.rationale: Invented name that press misspelled as 'Latches' in one Inman URL and that is confusable with the smart lock company Latch; no sourced press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Latchel grew quickly after YC, from 2,000 units in March 2018 to 27,500 by February 2019, raised a $2.3M seed in June 2019 and a $16.7M Series A led by F-Prime in July 2022, and now serves over 400 customers and more than 80,000 homes by its own count. It added an AI call center to its maintenance engine. No layoffs, sale or shutdown were found.
notes: FinTech Global (2022-07) says $24.3M total raised including a $2.3M seed led by Bain Capital Ventures and YC; Built In says $7.6M was raised in seed, pre-seed and angel rounds before the Series A; CB Insights says $50.9M. These do not reconcile, so only the two cited rounds are recorded and coverage is partial. The seed label comes from FinTech Global; Inman does not state a stage. Competitors list left empty: dated 2019 sources (TechCrunch, Inman) name none, and Property Meld appears only on an undated CB Insights page. YC lists founded 2016, Latka says 2019. Searches for layoffs or acquisition returned nothing about Latchel.
